change_note: 1.2.0 (M1-01b): acp_submit requires the idempotency key (high-entropy/namespaced, one global namespace per action), the HTTP manual legacy path documents missing-key = non-idempotent call with a permanent duplicate-task negative, read/status/prepare may never start computation, and the analysis capability projection/errors are frozen to registered|executable|unavailable.
scope: P1 control, artifact, idempotency and budget fields. P2 adds approval/budget accumulation in runtime/admission-approval.v1.json; this file stays the P1 subset. B12 freezes the ArtifactRef and the explicit prepare/read/analyze operation lifecycle. B15 adds the stdio proxy identity binding/permission ceiling and the project-scoped API-key revocation semantics; local-single stays the default.

expected_revision.description: CAS guard; a mismatch is conflict (revision_conflict).

project_id.description: rerun only; must equal the current project.

pause.local: SIGSTOP to the process group; the process stays registered (no memory/disk release)
pause.idempotent: pausing a paused task returns the current snapshot unchanged
pause.poller: a paused task is skipped by the poller but still counts as active (never deletable)

continue.attempt: attempt+1 in the same task directory
continue.target_node: optional re-pin; an unknown/incapable override is invalid-parameter

cancel.rule: cancelled is written only after the execution owner confirms the process/remote job stopped (EXECUTION PROTOCOL invariant 2)
cancel.terminal: a terminal record is returned unchanged with already_terminal=true

rerun.attempt: attempt+1, same task directory; the previous attempt receipt is archived under WORK/00_RUNTIME/attempts/<N>/

edit.exactly_once_rule: the same request_id replays the recorded result; a different payload under the same request_id is conflict

transition_rules: every write is one CAS through JobStore.transition (revision/status/attempt guards)
a control intent is never overwritten by a stale poll observation
a terminal state can never be resurrected by a stale write
terminal side effects run after the terminal CAS is persisted and are idempotent

prepare.wire_state_failed_alias: expired maps to ResourceState.failed on the wire (there is no expired wire value)

job_id.description: task id (also the path parameter); task_ref.task_id is accepted as the alias

relative_path.description: task-relative source path for a result artifact; absolute paths and parent traversal are invalid-parameter/path_traversal

expected_digest.description: trusted expected content digest; a mismatch is digest_mismatch and nothing is published

schema_ref.description: science schema id for an EvidenceReport artifact

source_refs.description: digested source references for an EvidenceReport artifact

evidence_report.description: A EvidenceReport document stored verbatim as an artifact; the platform does not interpret any claim

prepare.rule: prepare is explicit, idempotent, budget-checked and never triggered by a read or a list
prepare.no_implicit_compute: prepare may allocate/fetch/commit an artifact but never starts science (no QC task, no model call); if a purpose would need computation it is refused instead
rules: prepare is explicit, idempotent per (job, attempt, resource, content identity), budget-checked and never triggered by a read or a list
the same (job, attempt, resource, generation, expected digest) returns the same persistent operation ref; a different generation/digest/payload is a new operation
the operation is executed by the persistent prepare worker under the data_operations state machine, never inline in the route
a failed prepare is a named error (not_prepared/remote_cache_missing/digest_mismatch/path_traversal/permission_revoked), never an empty success

digest.description: artifact_ref.digest carried as the digest query on GET /api/v1/jobs/{job_id}/prepared/{artifact_id}

read.rule: a read never fetches; a miss is not-prepared (resource_not_ready) with retryable=true and a prepare hint
read.no_implicit_compute: read/status/prepare never start a calculation: no task, no attempt, no analysis. A read that would need a prepare returns not-prepared instead of enqueuing one.
read.digest_rule: the response digest MUST equal the requested artifact_ref.digest; a mismatch is conflict, never a silent serve
rules: a read never fetches (no SSH/SFTP), never enqueues a prepare and never parses or writes a body
a cache miss is resource_not_ready (not_prepared) with retryable=true and a prepare hint; it is never an empty body
a stale generation is revision_conflict/generation_stale; a cross-attempt read is revision_conflict/attempt_mismatch or not prepared
a digest mismatch or corrupt stored body is revision_conflict/digest_mismatch and zero bytes are served
a path traversal/unsafe token is input_invalid/path_traversal before any filesystem access

artifacts.generation_rule: task_id + attempt + artifact_id + generation + digest is the only verifiable artifact reference; any subset is insufficient
artifacts.path_rule: relative_path is task-relative; an absolute host path is never returned

artifact_ref.description: The only verifiable artifact reference. Every read validates all five identity fields and never serves on a partial match.

semantics.task: the durable task (job) identity; task_id is authoritative and job_id is its legacy alias for the same value (never a second task)
semantics.job: alias of task; a response emits task_ref.task_id and emits task_ref.job_id only while the legacy job row exists
semantics.attempt: 1-based attempt of that task; a body published for attempt N is never served for another attempt
semantics.resource: the prepared cache resource id; resource_id is the platform-derived name (artifact_id for purpose=artifact) and is never a client-chosen request field
semantics.artifact: the published artifact identity within the attempt (artifact_id); rerunning the producer increments generation instead of reusing the id
semantics.generation: monotonic revision of one artifact within one attempt; a newer generation supersedes older ones and an old generation read is revision_conflict/generation_stale
semantics.digest: sha256:<64 hex> over the artifact bytes (never plan_digest/proposal_digest/contract_digest); a mismatch is revision_conflict/digest_mismatch and zero bytes are served

relative_path.description: task-relative source path; an absolute host path is never returned

source_schema.description: science schema id when the bytes are an EvidenceReport; never interpreted by the platform

authorization.description: Inert projection of the boundary that admitted the operation; every request re-authorizes through entry_authz.

artifact_ref.identity_rule: job_id + attempt + resource_id + generation + digest is the only verifiable artifact reference; any subset is insufficient
artifact_ref.digest_rule: the served digest MUST equal the requested digest; a mismatch is revision_conflict/digest_mismatch and no bytes are served
artifact_ref.generation_rule: a newer generation supersedes older ones; an old generation read is revision_conflict/generation_stale
artifact_ref.attempt_rule: a body published for attempt N is never served for another attempt; cross-attempt reads are revision_conflict/attempt_mismatch or not prepared
artifact_ref.authorization_rule: a project-scope revocation/denial refuses prepare/read/analyze; the projection never widens access

operation.projection: PrepareOperation projection plus the frozen artifact_ref (when purpose=artifact)
operation.rule: never enqueues, leases, fetches, parses or mutates an operation

evidence_report.storage: opaque bytes published as an artifact; schema_ref and source_refs are recorded verbatim
evidence_report.read: bytes are served unchanged and verified by digest; no claim field is added
evidence_report.platform_rule: the platform never interprets an EvidenceReport as claim supported; claim status remains exactly what A wrote
evidence_report.registration_owner: B18 owns the evidence registration mapping; B12 owns storage/read only

idempotency.scope: one key per (resolved principal, command, key). A key from another principal is a different operation.
idempotency.key_source: client-supplied; the pre-M0-05 server derivation (sha256 over plan_digest, entry id, resolved principal) survives only as a read-only lookup namespace for historical local-single rows

missing_key_result.side_effects: none: no task, no attempt, no reservation, no ledger row

mcp_submit.entropy_rule: the raw key is a GLOBAL namespace per action (across projects, principals and entries), so a client MUST send a high-entropy UUID or a namespaced key that embeds project/research/round (e.g. '<client>:<project>:<round>:<call>'). A short human key is never safe.

short_key_cross_tenant_result.rule: two tenants that reuse one short key are a typed conflict to reconcile, never a replay of the other tenant's operation

mcp_submit.actionable_message: reuse the key with the identical request, or mint a new namespaced key; do not rename the payload under the same key

http_manual_legacy.contract_statement: MISSING KEY = NON-IDEMPOTENT CALL. The HTTP manual/legacy submit path may omit the key (hand-run operators, pre-M1 scripts); such a call is explicitly non-idempotent: a retry may create a SECOND task.
never: silently deriving a submit key for a caller that omitted it
treating a retry of a key-less call as a replay
reporting idempotent_replay=true for a key-less call

key_policy.samples_rule: the short-key cross-tenant conflict and the key-less duplicate-task case are permanent negatives; removing either re-opens the 'silent compatibility' failure M1-01b closed

window.note: the replay record lives in the Controller store, never in a process-local dict

rules.outcome: return the recorded operation_ref with idempotent_replay=true; create nothing
refused with invalid-parameter/input_invalid (params.rule=idempotency_key_required); nothing is created
allowed and explicitly NON-IDEMPOTENT: a retry may create a second task; the response never reports idempotent_replay=true

rules.case: one short key reused by two tenants
rules.outcome: conflict (revision_conflict, params.rule=idempotency_scope_conflict); the second caller never receives the first caller's task
the key still deduplicates (no in-connection state authority)

mode.description: AdmissionMode. quota-only is the research baseline; usage-only must be explicitly requested.

rules: admission precedes execution and happens once per attempt
a reservation is released when the attempt reaches a terminal state or is refused before execution
metering is decoupled: a metering failure never changes scientific completion, readability or the job terminal state
a duplicate or out-of-order receipt never double-meters
the budget ledger is the only resource authority; a tool must never hold a local budget counter as authority (GAP-B03-03)
cumulative/reservation settlement is P2 and is specified in runtime/admission-approval.v1.json

denied_quota.note: a budget refusal is a policy decision, not a transient error

capability_states.projection: acp_capabilities.analysis_capabilities[]: one entry per frozen analysis id with {analysis_id, state, registered, executable, version, owner}; there is deliberately no available/ready state
capability_states.executable: registered AND a handler exists; only this state may run
capability_states.registered: declared without a handler: analyze refuses it with unsupported_capability
capability_states.unavailable: not registered at all: analyze refuses it with unsupported_capability
capability_states.rule: advertising a capability descriptor is never an execution promise

error_freeze.reads_existing_evidence: vibration.analyze reads prepared evidence only and never starts QC; vibration.compute starts exactly one frequency task and requires plan_digest

analyze.rule: explicit-only and registry-gated; until A registers a capability handler exactly zero science is started and no task/prepare is created

registered_not_executable_result.note: a declared capability without a handler; the projection reports state=registered and analyze refuses it instead of starting science

stdio_identity.multi_user_requires: ACP_IDENTITY_MODE=api-key and a Controller-verified API key

revocation.key: the next request and the next event-stream poll re-read the key row
revocation.account: the account status is re-read, key refs are revoked and open streams are rechecked
